items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: Cat said, 'Eldridge, you take this part.' ... Cat had five trumpets.

ctx.x: Pullman cars they'd be playing cards and talking about me. "Won't never be nothin'," you know, like that. And I hadn't been there twelve hours when they said I had my hand in the man's pocket.

There were some funny things happened. Like, they finally tricked me, the first trumpet player... They found out I couldn't read. Because I was playing all them marches and classical tunes that they played, but by ear, you know. So the first trumpet player purposely stayed on. We were trapped in the Pullman car, and he stayed in there after (?). Cat said, "Eldridge, you take this part." Cat had five trumpets. Why give it to me? But that was to psych me out, to see whether I could read or not, you know. And I'll…

So he tapped, he said, "Okay, hit it now," and he gives the downbeat, and no first trumpet. "Let's try it again." So I still was trying to fake it. I said, "I think somebody's not reading their part right." He said, "Well, you play your part..." [LAUGHS] That's where they got me, you know. So then I was really in bad shape around them.
